title: The Couple Reading

intake.question: How long have you been together?
What do you two argue about most?
What do you want from this reading?

options.label: To think about the long term

plan.title: How you love (and what you never say)
What your chemistry is actually made of
What each of you brings to the table
How you two fight, and how you make up
Your story so far, read back to you
What home feels like with you two
How you grow together without growing apart

strong.text:
Yeon: Strong chart. You love like you lead: full force, clear direction, your way.

Bom: You make them feel so safe.

Yeon: And sometimes a little steamrolled. "I booked it already" is romantic twice. The tenth time it's a policy.

Once this week, let them pick. The restaurant, the film, the plan. Then enjoy it out loud, even if it's not what you'd have chosen.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You love at full volume. Check if they can hear themselves think.

weak.text:
Bom: Your chart runs soft. You love by tuning in: their mood, their week, what they need before they ask.

Yeon: And you put yourself last so smoothly nobody notices you did it.

Bom: Your needs aren't an inconvenience to the relationship. They're half of it.

This week, ask for one specific thing. Not "whatever you want". One thing you want.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You give so gently. Let them give back.

strong.text:
Yeon: Strong chart, so you fight to resolve. Sometimes to win. Your intensity can flatten someone who needs a minute.

Bom: House rule: whoever's calmer speaks second, and nobody decides anything in the first twenty minutes.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: No final decisions in the first twenty minutes. Heat writes bad verdicts.

weak.text:
Bom: Soft chart, so you fight by retreating or giving in. It feels like keeping the peace.

Yeon: It mostly keeps the problem. Wrapped nicely.

Bom: Write your side down before the talk, so the words are there even when your nerve leaves.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Notes app before the talk. The words stay when your nerve goes.

strong.text:
Yeon: Strong chart, so you tend to drive the couple's growth. Plans, goals, moves. Usually from the driver's seat.

Bom: Share the steering. Let them choose the next big adventure, even if you'd have picked something else.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Hand them the wheel for the next adventure. No backseat driving.

weak.text:
Bom: Soft chart, so you might follow their growth more than you lead your own.

Yeon: Their promotion, their marathon, their sourdough phase. What's yours?

Bom: Pick one thing for yourself this year and ask them to back it. Couples grow best when both people do.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Pick one thing that's just yours this year. Ask them to cheer.

strong.text:
Yeon: Strong chart over decades: habits that only one of you chose quietly become "how we do things".

Bom: Every few years, renegotiate the basics. Who does what, where you live, how holidays work. Keep it belonging to both of you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Renegotiate every few years. New terms, same two people.

weak.text:
Bom: Soft chart over decades: you can quietly fade into the relationship.

Yeon: Not dramatically. Just one skipped hobby and one cancelled friend at a time.

Bom: Keep investing in you. Friends, health, ambitions. They fell for a whole person. Stay one.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Keep your own life. That's who they fell for.

peer_strong.text:
You've kept a mental tally of who did the last three food shops. Don't deny it.

Your chart is stacked with {dm_el}, your own element. Saju calls it the peer family: equals, and a little bit rivals.

Bom: You need a partner beside you. Not above, not below. Shared decisions, fair splits.

Yeon: Which is how "who's more tired" becomes a competitive sport in your house.

Bom: The gift: you never vanish into the relationship. The work: letting closeness feel like a team, not a scoreboard.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Equal partners. Now stop counting who's more tired.

output_strong.text:
You're the one who turns a Tuesday into a theme night. Then rolls your eyes at the chore rota.

Your chart is stacked with {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} pours out. Saju calls it the output family: expression, play, affection.

Bom: You make ordinary days memorable. That's a real gift in a couple.

Yeon: You also treat house rules like a personal insult.

Bom: Put the fun inside the routine. A silly ritual. A Friday surprise. Laundry with a soundtrack.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your {heavy_el} makes home playful. Turn the boring bits into a game.

wealth_strong.text:
You've researched the best mattress for both of you. Twice. With a spreadsheet.

Your chart is stacked with {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} manages. Saju calls it the wealth family: building, providing, sorting things out.

Yeon: You show love by making life run. Booked, paid, organised, done.

Bom: They love that. They'd also love you, sitting still, doing nothing useful, next to them.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Providing is love. So is one useless hour on the sofa together.

power_strong.text:
You have rules for how towels get folded. They were never discussed. They are, however, enforced.

Your chart is stacked with {heavy_el}, the element that presses on your {dm_el}. Saju calls it the power family: duty, standards, taking commitment seriously.

Bom: You're loyal and responsible. People feel safe with you.

Yeon: You also hold them to rules they never signed.

Bom: Say your expectations out loud. Unspoken rules are the ones that get broken.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Write the rules down together. Secret rules aren't fair rules.

resource_strong.text:
You knew they needed a night off three days before they did. You still haven't booked it.

Your chart is stacked with {heavy_el}, the element that feeds your {dm_el}. Saju calls it the resource family: comfort, insight, understanding.

Bom: You're the thoughtful one. Quiet nights, deep talks, someone who gets it.

Yeon: You understand everything and act on about half of it.

Bom: Turn the knowing into doing. If you know they need rest, book the rest.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You already know what they need. Do it before they ask.

output_weak.text:
You've handed out effort like free samples all week. Now you're on the sofa, empty, wondering why.

Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} gives away: affection, help, care.

Bom: You pour and pour. It's lovely to be loved by you.

Yeon: You also flinch when someone gives back. "Oh, you didn't have to." They wanted to.

Bom: Let them give back. Receiving well is half of a balanced relationship.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Let them give back. Just say "thank you" and stop there.

wealth_weak.text:
You're the family calendar, the budget and the person who knows where the passports are. Also very tired.

Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} has to manage. A lot to handle, not much backup.

Yeon: You carry the admin of the whole relationship and call it "just easier if I do it".

Bom: Split the load out loud. On paper, if it helps. Then actually hand some of it over.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Write down who does what. You'll gasp at your half.

power_weak.text:
They said "you left the light on". You heard "you're a disappointment as a human". Sound familiar?

Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element that presses on your {dm_el}: pressure and judgement.

Bom: You try so hard to be a good partner. Criticism lands heavier on you than it's meant.

Yeon: Choose warm over harsh. And tell them gentle notes work best on you. That's not fragile. That's instructions.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Ask for feedback with kindness on it. Fair request.

rooted_on_paper.text:
Everyone thinks you're the steady one. You are. You also lie awake wondering if they're still sure about you.

Bom: Both are true. Calm outside, needing reassurance inside.

Yeon: So tell them which kind works. A hug? A text at lunch? A plan for next month? They're not psychic.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Steady outside, unsure inside. Tell them which reassurance works.

output_strong.text:
{miss_el} doesn't show in your chart, and for your {dm_el} that's the "saying it out loud" element.

Yeon: You love in actions. You fixed the shelf. You think that covered "I love you" for the month.

Bom: They might need the words. One sentence a day about what you appreciate. That's the whole fix.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Actions are lovely. Words count too. One a day.

wealth_strong.text:
{miss_el} doesn't show in your chart, and for your {dm_el} that's the "make plans happen" element.

Yeon: Big talk about the trip. No dates. Two years running.

Bom: Pick one shared goal a year and make it real. Dates, tickets, a jar for it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: One real plan a year. On the fridge. With a date on it.

power_strong.text:
{miss_el} doesn't show in your chart, and for your {dm_el} that's the structure element.

Bom: You love freely and generously.

Yeon: And you forget to text when you're running an hour late. Every time. Like it's a surprise every time.

Bom: The small promises are what make someone feel safe. Keep those first.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Text when you're late. That's romance with good manners.

resource_strong.text:
{miss_el} doesn't show in your chart, and for your {dm_el} that's the "being looked after" element.

Yeon: Offer you soup when you're ill and you'll say "I'm fine" through a fever.

Bom: Accept the care. It's a gift to them too. They want to be useful to you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Take the soup. Say thanks. Survive it.

output_weak.text:
{miss_el} doesn't show in your chart, and for your {dm_el} that's the "expressing it" element.

Bom: It protects you from giving yourself away. It also makes you hard to read.

Yeon: They're looking at your face for clues. Your face is giving them nothing.

Bom: Small signs carry a lot. A hand on their arm. A note in their bag. A song you sent "for no reason".

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: A note, a touch, a song. Small signs do heavy lifting.

wealth_weak.text:
{miss_el} doesn't show in your chart, and for your {dm_el} that's the "taking the lead" element.

Yeon: They pick the holiday, the flat, the restaurant. You say "sounds good" and then have opinions in the taxi.

Bom: Lead one thing this year. Start to finish. Your call.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You plan the next trip. All of it. No "whatever you think".

power_weak.text:
{miss_el} doesn't show in your chart, and for your {dm_el} that's the outside-pressure element. Fewer rules weighing on you. Nice.

Bom: It also means you're not sure what's fair to ask for.

Yeon: Respect, consistency, kindness. That's not a big ask. That's the minimum.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Asking for respect isn't high maintenance. It's the floor.

resource_weak.text:
{miss_el} doesn't show in your chart, and for your {dm_el} that's the support element. You run on willpower.

Yeon: Willpower and iced coffee. Mostly coffee.

Bom: Let your partner into your refill routine on purpose. And keep friends who top you up too.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Willpower isn't a support system. They can be.

none_strong.text:
Every one of the five elements turns up in your chart. On a strong chart that's range: fun, steady, romantic, practical. You can be all of it.

Yeon: And you try to be. For them. All at once.

Bom: Let them be good at something for you. Even if you could do it better.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You could do it all. Let them do some of it.

none_weak.text:
Your chart holds all five elements. On a soft chart that's flexibility: you can fit almost any partner.

Yeon: "Fit" is doing a lot of work there. Are you fitting, or disappearing?

Bom: Say your preference first sometimes. Before you've checked theirs.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Flexible isn't invisible. Say what you want first.

resource.title: What steadies you two: {helper_el}
resource.text:
Every chart has an element that brings it back to balance. Your soft {dm_el} chart steadies with {helper_el}, the one that feeds you.

Bom: In love, that means being nurtured. Rest. A partner who looks after you. Friends who refill you.

Yeon: Love from a full cup. Not from the last drop at the bottom of the mug.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: {helper_el} refills you. Love from a full mug, not the dregs.

peer.title: What steadies you two: {helper_el}, your own element
peer.text:
Every chart has an element that brings it back to balance. Yours already has plenty feeding it, so what steadies you is your own element, {helper_el}.

Bom: In love, that means friendship. A partner who's also your best mate.

Yeon: And friends outside the couple who'll tell you when you're being ridiculous.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: {helper_el} steadies you: date your best friend.

output.title: What balances you two: {helper_el}
output.text:
Every chart has an element that brings it back to balance. A strong {dm_el} chart needs an outlet, and yours is {helper_el}, the element you pour out.

Yeon: In love, that means play. Fun. Being generous with your time and silliness.

Bom: Spend your strength on fun together instead of on control. Same amount of you, much better results.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Your outlet is {helper_el}: play together, not control.

wealth.title: What balances you two: {helper_el}
wealth.text:
Every chart has an element that brings it back to balance. Yours is strong and expressive, so what balances you is {helper_el}, the element you shape.

Bom: In love, that means building something real together. A home, a ritual, a shared project with an end date.

Yeon: Something you can point at and say "we did that". Ideally not a fight.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your balance is {helper_el}: build something you can point at.

wood.text: Wood for you two looks like: walks somewhere green, a herb pot on the windowsill, learning something new side by side.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Wood for you two: green walks, a plant, a class together.

fire.text: Fire for you two looks like: warm evenings with friends, sunshine, celebrations, trips to bright places, laughing too loud.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Fire for you two: friends, sun, a reason to celebrate.

earth.text: Earth for you two looks like: a cosy home, cooking together, family meals, staying in on purpose.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Earth for you two: cosy home, cooking, staying in.

metal.text: Metal for you two looks like: clear agreements, a tidy shared space, honest talks, promises kept to the minute.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Metal for you two: clear deals, kept exactly.

water.text: Water for you two looks like: long talks, quiet nights, time near water, and space for each of you to think.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Water for you two: long talks and room to think.

rat.text: Your day branch is the Rat (子), midnight Water, a charm branch. At home you live for inside jokes and late talks, and you guard your privacy. Pick someone who doesn't take that personally.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Rat at home: late talks, inside jokes, a closed door sometimes.

ox.text: Your day branch is the Ox (丑), cold Earth that stores Metal. At home you're devoted and in it for years, and completely certain about the right way to load the dishwasher.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Ox at home: loyal for decades, wrong about nothing. Allegedly.

tiger.text: Your day branch is the Tiger (寅), early spring Wood. At home you need freedom and a partner who says yes to the spontaneous plan. Feel caged and you'll pace.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Tiger at home: commitment with the door open.

rabbit.text: Your day branch is the Rabbit (卯), spring Wood, a charm branch. At home you want gentleness: soft light, soft words. A harsh fight stays with you for days.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Rabbit at home: be gentle, or be remembered.

dragon.text: Your day branch is the Dragon (辰), damp Earth that stores Water. At home you dream big for the two of you, and you need someone who takes those dreams seriously.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Dragon at home: big dreams, said out loud.

snake.text: Your day branch is the Snake (巳), early summer Fire. At home you open slowly, then completely. Trust is the whole thing.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Snake at home: one key, handed over once.

horse.text: Your day branch is the Horse (午), midsummer Fire, a charm branch. At home you want warmth, noise and freedom, and nobody holding the reins.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Horse at home: warm, loud, never fenced in.

goat.text: Your day branch is the Goat (未), warm late-summer Earth. At home you want cosy and creative, with a kind, patient partner.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Goat at home: blankets, crafts, zero rushing.

monkey.text: Your day branch is the Monkey (申), early autumn Metal. At home you need banter and someone who keeps your brain busy.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Monkey at home: keep the jokes coming.

rooster.text: Your day branch is the Rooster (酉), autumn Metal, a charm branch. At home you love order and beauty, and a partner who notices the details.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Rooster at home: the frame is straight. You checked.

dog.text: Your day branch is the Dog (戌), dry autumn Earth that keeps Fire. At home you're fiercely loyal, and you need that loyalty back in full.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Dog at home: devotion both ways, or not at all.

pig.text: Your day branch is the Pig (亥), early winter Water. At home you're generous and easy, happiest with simple pleasures shared.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Pig at home: full fridge, soft sofa, good company.

day_branch_heading: How you live at home: the {day_animal} ({day_branch})

new.text:
Under a year in. You still tidy before they come over. You still pretend you like their friend's band.

Bom: This is when you set the tone for how you treat each other tired, hungry and stressed.

Yeon: The fight patterns from the last chapter? They're coming. Talk about them now, while they're still funny.

Bom: Be a little kinder than you need to on the bad days. Whatever you do now becomes the default.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Kind on the bad days now means kind on the bad days later.

settled.text:
One to three years. The hoodie has migrated permanently. You know their "work voice" and you know their "hungry voice".

Yeon: This is when couples pick their fight habits for the next ten years. Usually without noticing.

Bom: So pick on purpose. And talk about the big stuff while it's calm: where to live, money, what weekends look like.

Yeon: Talk now, or argue about it in a car park in 2031.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your fight habits are setting like concrete. Choose them now.

long.text:
Three years or more. You can tell their mood from how they say "hey". You have a whole language nobody else speaks.

Bom: This reading might name something you've both felt for years and never said.

Yeon: Use it. Have the conversation you've been postponing since roughly the second Christmas.

Bom: And do one brand-new thing together this month. It reminds you both there's still more to find.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Have the talk you keep moving to "next weekend".

committed.text:
Engaged or married. You've promised the long version, in front of people.

Bom: The long-run chapter at the end is the one to read slowly. And the home chapter is your household weather report.

Yeon: Also, families are now officially involved. Talk about holidays and in-laws before the next big one, not in the car on the way there.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Sort the holiday plan before the holiday. Not on the motorway.

unsaid.text:
You didn't say how long. Fine. Week six or year twelve, these patterns are already running your days.

Yeon: Here's a plan. Two phones, one sofa, this reading. Argue about which bits are true.

Bom: Then each pick one chapter to talk about over dinner. Beats "how was your day".

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: One sofa, two phones. Argue about the details.

time.text:
Your answer: time and attention. One of you is counting hours together. The other is counting phone checks at dinner.

Bom: Underneath, it's about feeling like a priority.

Yeon: Protect one ritual that nothing interrupts. A weekly dinner. One phone-free hour. Sacred.

Bom: Also, some people want long stretches together, others want lots of little check-ins. Neither's wrong. They just need translating.

Yeon: And where you two live day to day decides a lot of this. That's next.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Time fights are priority fights. Guard one ritual.

logistics.text:
You said chores, plans and money stuff. So, the "who booked the vet" Cold War.

Bom: It's about fairness and feeling respected. Every time.

Yeon: Write down who does what. Review it every few months. Yes, like a contract. A romantic contract.

Bom: And thank each other for the boring stuff. "Thanks for doing the bins" costs nothing and fixes more than you'd think.

Yeon: Next: what home actually feels like for you two. It's where most of these fights are born.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: It's never the chore. It's the fairness. Make the list.

feelings.text:
You said feelings and communication. "It's not what you said, it's how you said it" has been spoken in your home. Recently.

Bom: Try this: repeat back what you heard before you answer. Half these fights end right there.

Yeon: And agree on a silly pause word. "Pineapple." Either of you says it, twenty minutes apart, then back.

Bom: Next chapter is home: the rooms where these conversations actually happen.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Mirror their words first. Then reply. Then "pineapple" if needed.

people.text:
You said friends or family. The fight about someone who isn't in the room and would be horrified to know.

Yeon: It's about loyalty. Whose side are you on.

Bom: Agree that in front of others, you're a team. Disagree privately, later, at home.

Yeon: Set a few rules together on how often you see each side. A clear plan beats arguing case by case.

Bom: Speaking of home, that's the next chapter. What it feels like to live with the two of you.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: In public, a team. The debate happens at home.

unsaid.text:
No fight topic from you. Every couple has a favourite topic, though. Watch for yours this month.

Bom: It usually points straight at what each of you needs most.

Yeon: Fights are information. Annoying, loud information.

Bom: Next: home, and what living side by side actually feels like for you two.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your favourite fight topic is a map. Read it.

understand.text:
You said you want to understand them better. So here's homework, the fun kind.

Bom: Read their chapter out loud to them. Ask which bits are true. Their answers will teach you more than any chart.

Yeon: Then hand them yours. Brace for "oh, that's SO you". You'll learn how you look from the outside.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Read their chapter to them. Ask what's true. Listen.

fight.text:
You said you want to fight less. Good. Don't try ten things.

Yeon: Pick one tip from the fight chapter. Both of you. One month.

Bom: And end every argument with one thing you appreciate about each other.

Yeon: Cheesy. Embarrassing. Annoyingly effective.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: One tip, one month, both of you. Cheesy works.

future.text:
You said you want to think about the long term. Then make it a conversation, not a vibe.

Bom: Use the last few chapters to talk about the next five years. Where, how, with what.

Yeon: Write it down. Revisit it next year. Include the fun stuff, not just the boring adult bits. Trips. Hobbies. A dog called something stupid.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Write down your next five years. Put a trip in it.

fun.text:
You said you're just curious. Perfect. Our favourite kind of reader.

Yeon: Read the spicy bits out loud. Fight about which of you is more stubborn. It's you. It's always the one reading.

Bom: Then compare with your friends' couples and decide which pair would survive a reality show.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Just curious? Decide who's more stubborn. Out loud.

unsaid.text:
You didn't pick a goal for this. Maybe it shows up by the end.

Bom: Find the one line that stung or made you smile. Tell them about it tonight.

Yeon: That's it. That's the whole assignment. If you talk about it, this did its job.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Send them the line that hit hardest. Conversation started.

wood.heading: What you need from love: to feel it growing
wood.text:
Yeon: You don't need fireworks. You need a direction. A trip on the calendar. A "next year we should".

Bom: Standing still scares you more than fighting.

Yeon: Which is why you start "where is this going" talks at completely random moments. Like during dessert.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Talk about your future together. It calms you more than you admit.

fire.heading: What you need from love: to feel lit up
fire.text:
Bom: You need warmth you can see. Eye contact. Excitement. Them lighting up when you walk in.

Yeon: If they say "nice" in a flat voice about something you're thrilled about, you'll think about it for a week.

Bom: Ask them to show it. Out loud. It's allowed.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: "Nice." The most dangerous word you can say to a Fire person.

earth.heading: What you need from love: to feel safe
earth.text:
Bom: You need steadiness. Same person on Tuesday as on Saturday. Plans that actually happen.

Yeon: Last-minute cancellations hit you harder than any fight.

Bom: Tell them that. "Consistency is how I feel loved" is a full sentence.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Consistency is your love language. Say it out loud once.

metal.heading: What you need from love: to feel respected
metal.text:
Yeon: You need respect before romance. Keep your word, and you're theirs forever. Break it once, and you'll remember the date.

Bom: You show love by being reliable. You need it back the same way.

Yeon: Also, you want to be taken seriously. Laugh at the wrong moment and you'll go very, very quiet.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You can forgive a lot. A broken promise goes in the permanent file.

water.heading: What you need from love: to feel understood
water.text:
Bom: You need someone who gets the layers. Not just what you said. What you meant.

Yeon: You'll test it, too. A vague "I'm fine" to see if they notice it wasn't.

Bom: Try saying the actual thing. Being understood is easier when you're also being clear.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: "I'm fine" is not a puzzle they signed up to solve.

gap-wood.heading: Who they are: the Tall Pine
gap-wood.text:
They have a spreadsheet for the holiday and a backup plan for the backup plan. When they say "I'll sort it", it gets sorted.

Bom: That's how a Pine says "I love you". In bookings, repairs and kept promises.

Yeon: Not in poems. Do not wait for the poem.

Bom: What they never say: they'd love, just once, to be the one who gets looked after.

Yeon: So take one thing off their list without asking. Watch them not know what to do with their hands. (Saju calls them Gap Wood.)

eul-wood.heading: Who they are: the Climbing Flower
eul-wood.text:
They text "home safe?" every single time. They remembered the name of your awful coworker. They have never once started a fight in public.

Bom: They love by weaving you in. Your friends, your songs, your Sunday.

Yeon: And they read every hint like a crime scene. Say what you mean. Literally. Out loud.

Bom: What they never say: they bend too far to keep things nice, and then feel a bit lost.

Yeon: Tell them "you're chosen" in plain words. They'll pretend it's no big deal and screenshot it in their head. (Saju calls them Eul Wood.)

byeong-fire.heading: Who they are: the Sun
byeong-fire.text:
They planned your birthday three weeks early. They told the waiter it was your anniversary. It wasn't.

Bom: They love loudly and forgive fast. Warmth you can feel from the car park.

Yeon: They also flare up fast. And if you say "cool" in a flat voice about their big idea, they'll hear it for a week.

Bom: What they never say: the sun runs out too. They want to be celebrated back.

Yeon: Match their volume once in a while. Gasp. Clap. Overreact. It costs you nothing and buys you a month. (Saju calls them Byeong Fire.)

jeong-fire.heading: Who they are: the Candle
jeong-fire.text:
They noticed you went quiet at dinner. They didn't say anything. They brought you tea at 10pm and waited.

Bom: They love close and quiet. They remember the thing you said once, in passing, in March.

Yeon: When they're hurt they don't shout. They get polite. Polite is the alarm.

Bom: What they never say: they're giving far more than they show, and they'd love some of it back.

Yeon: Ask "how are you, actually?" and then sit there through the awkward pause. The real answer comes after it. (Saju calls them Jeong Fire.)

mu-earth.heading: Who they are: the Mountain
mu-earth.text:
You've had a crisis. They've had a sandwich and a plan. Nothing rattles them, and you've started to think nothing reaches them either.

Bom: It does. They just process it slowly, somewhere deep, without a soundtrack.

Yeon: Ask them a feelings question and you'll get a weather report. Wait ten minutes. The real answer arrives later, usually in the car.

Bom: What they never say: they get lonely when nobody asks how they really are.

Yeon: So ask. Then thank them for being steady, by name. Steady people almost never get thanked. (Saju calls them Mu Earth.)

gi-earth.heading: Who they are: the Garden Field
gi-earth.text:
There are snacks in your bag you didn't pack. Your plants are alive and you've never watered them. Mystery solved.

Bom: They love by tending. Meals, reminders, tiny rescues you don't even clock.

Yeon: And they swallow every small annoyance until one wet towel on the floor sets off the whole speech.

Bom: What they never say: they worry they're not enough, and they need looking after too.

Yeon: Notice one thing they did today and say it out loud. "You did the bins." Romance, Garden-style. (Saju calls them Gi Earth.)

gyeong-metal.heading: Who they are: the Sword
gyeong-metal.text:
They told you the haircut wasn't great. Then they told off the hairdresser. Both, within an hour. That's the whole package.

Bom: They love by being loyal and honest. Nobody gets to you while they're around.

Yeon: Their honesty arrives with no bubble wrap. They think hinting is lying.

Bom: What they never say: the armour is heavy. They want one place to put it down.

Yeon: Be that place. And when they finally go soft for a second, do not make a joke about it. They'll put the armour straight back on. (Saju calls them Gyeong Metal.)

sin-metal.heading: Who they are: the Jewel
sin-metal.text:
They chose the restaurant, the table and probably your outfit. The card they wrote you has no crossed-out words. They drafted it.

Bom: They love with care. Every gesture is considered, polished, meant.

Yeon: When you get it wrong, they don't yell. They go cool. Arctic, but polite.

Bom: What they never say: one careless comment scratches deeper than you'd ever guess.

Yeon: Compliment something specific. Not "you look nice". "That colour on you is unfair." They'll keep it forever. (Saju calls them Sin Metal.)

im-water.heading: Who they are: the Ocean
im-water.text:
They booked a train to a town neither of you can pronounce. Then they disappeared into a documentary for a whole Saturday. Same person. Same week.

Bom: They love deep and curious. Life with them keeps getting bigger.

Yeon: Grab on too tight and they drift. When they're upset, they don't fight. They go for a very long walk.

Bom: What they never say: they want a harbour more than they'd ever admit.

Yeon: Give them room, and be easy to come back to. That combo is rarer than you think. (Saju calls them Im Water.)

gye-water.heading: Who they are: the Rain
gye-water.text:
They knew you'd had a bad day from how you put your keys down. They said nothing and ordered your favourite food.

Bom: They love by sensing. Comfort, timing, the right thing before you asked.

Yeon: They also say "I'm fine" in a voice that is clearly not fine. And then wait to see if you noticed.

Bom: What they never say: sometimes they lose themselves in you and need help staying whole.

Yeon: Ask direct questions. "Are you upset with me?" is not rude to the Rain. It's a rescue. (Saju calls them Gye Water.)

strong.heading: How much room they take up
strong.text:
Their chart is built strong. Translation: they know what they want, and they go and get it.

Bom: Easy to lean on. Very easy.

Yeon: Also easy to forget you had an opinion. They'll pick the film before you've opened your mouth.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Say what you think early. A strong chart can't hear what you never said.

weak.heading: How much room they take up
weak.text:
Their chart is built soft. They read the room fast, adapt faster, and ask for very little.

Yeon: "Whatever you like" is their catchphrase. It's a lie about forty percent of the time.

Bom: Ask twice. The second answer is the real one.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: "I don't mind" means they mind. Ask again.

spring.heading: The season they were born in: spring
spring.text:
They were born in spring, so they love beginnings. New plans, new places, the first week of anything.

Yeon: If the relationship stops moving, they get twitchy. They'll suddenly want to repaint the bathroom.

Bom: Keep starting small things together. A class, a recipe, a route home.

Yeon: Next chapter: what they actually are to you. Saju has a name for it, and it explains a lot about your last argument.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Spring people need a "next". Give them one.

summer.heading: The season they were born in: summer
summer.text:
They were born in summer, so they run warm. Expressive, social, all in.

Yeon: They also go from zero to boiling in one sentence. And back down in twenty minutes, like nothing happened.

Bom: Give them a cool-off window. Don't take the heat as the verdict.

Bom: Next: what the two of you are, chemically. One of you is the spark and one is the fuel. You'll know which.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Hot fast, cool fast. Wait twenty minutes before replying.

autumn.heading: The season they were born in: autumn
autumn.text:
They were born in autumn, so they're clear-eyed. They know what they like, and they say it.

Yeon: "Is that what you're wearing?" can be a genuine question from an autumn person. Mostly.

Bom: Ask what they meant before you take it personally. It's usually precision, not judgement.

Yeon: Next chapter is your chemistry. Spoiler: it explains why their "small notes" land so loud on you.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Precise, not critical. Ask what they meant first.

winter.heading: The season they were born in: winter
winter.text:
They were born in winter, so they warm up slowly. Then completely.

Yeon: Their silence is not a review of you. They're just thinking. For a long time.

Bom: Be patient with the quiet. It's where they keep the good stuff.

Bom: Next: what they are to you in saju. It's the reason you can sit in a room with them and say nothing for an hour.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Quiet isn't distance. It's loading.

earth.heading: The season they were born in: the in-between weeks
earth.text:
They were born in the Earth weeks between seasons. They're the calm one when everything changes: moves, new jobs, bad news.

Yeon: Which means everyone leans on them. Including you. Especially you.

Bom: Let them lean back sometimes. The steady one needs a wall too.

Yeon: Next chapter: what your chemistry is made of. Prepare to feel very seen, and slightly called out.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: They're your calm in a storm. Be theirs once.

0.heading: What they are to you: the best friend (比肩)
0.text:
You finish each other's sentences. You also both reach for the last dumpling at the exact same second.

Bom: {them} is your Friend in saju's ten roles. Same element, same style. A best friend you also happen to fancy.

Yeon: Mirrors double everything. Two stubborn people, zero people bending.

Bom: You rarely feel misunderstood with them. That's huge.

Yeon: Decide in advance who gets the final word on what. Holidays: you. Sofa: them. Saves a war.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You get each other without a translator. Rare. Keep it.

1.heading: What they are to you: the rival sibling (劫財)
1.text:
You've turned Monopoly into a blood sport. You've argued about which way the toilet roll goes like it was a court case. And it's honestly kind of hot.

Yeon: {them} is your Rival Sibling in saju's ten roles. Same element, opposite style. Sibling banter with a crush on top.

Bom: You make each other sharper. You get better because the other one is watching.

Yeon: The danger is competing at home. Who's more tired. Who gave up more. Who's "always" the one.

Bom: Point the rivalry outward. You two against the world, not against each other in the kitchen.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Say "you were right" once. No sarcasm. Watch them fall over.

2.heading: What they are to you: the joy (食神)
2.text:
You make them laugh without trying. You cook, they glow. You encourage, they bloom.

Bom: {them} is your Joy in saju's ten roles. Your element feeds theirs, and it feels like play, not work.

Yeon: Feeding someone is lovely. Until you realise you haven't eaten in three years. Metaphorically.

Bom: Ask for one specific thing a week. They'll be thrilled to finally know what you want.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Giving to them feels easy. Let some of it come back to you.

3.heading: What they are to you: the spark (傷官)
3.text:
Your conversations go off like popcorn. You bring out their wild side. They bring out your bluntest opinions.

Yeon: {them} is your Spark in saju's ten roles. Your element feeds theirs, with a twist. Electric. Very talkative.

Bom: They're more themselves around you than anywhere else.

Yeon: The risk is you, holding a list of how they could be better. And reading it out.

Bom: Praise twice for every correction. The same sentence lands as a gift or a cut depending on whether it's the fourth note today.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Two compliments per critique. That's the exchange rate.

4.heading: What they are to you: the adventure (偏財)
4.text:
They're the one who says "let's just go" at 9pm on a Tuesday. And somehow you go.

Bom: {them} is your Adventure in saju's ten roles. Your element shapes theirs. They make life feel bigger.

Yeon: The chase was thrilling. The danger is acting like the chase is over because you won.

Bom: Keep courting them. Years in. Plan the surprise even when you already "have" them.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You caught them. Keep choosing them anyway.

5.heading: What they are to you: the life partner (正財)
5.text:
You have a shared calendar. You've discussed sofas with real emotion. You are, frankly, extremely good at being a couple.

Yeon: {them} is your Partner in saju's ten roles. Your element shapes theirs. The classic build-a-life pairing.

Bom: Practical, loyal, a future with actual dates in it.

Yeon: The risk is becoming brilliant flatmates who forget to flirt.

Bom: One evening a week with zero logistics. No bills, no plans, no "did you call the plumber".

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Excellent flatmates. Now flirt like you're not.

6.heading: What they are to you: the challenge (七殺)
6.text:
They get under your skin like nobody else. You've never grown faster, or argued louder, than with this person.

Bom: {them} is your Challenge in saju's ten roles. Their element presses on yours. The most intense of all ten.

Yeon: Passion with pressure. Magnetic and a bit exhausting.

Bom: Intensity only feels good when both of you feel safe inside it.

Yeon: So agree on how you fight before you fight. Rules first, fireworks second.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Intense is fine. Unsafe isn't. Know the difference.

7.heading: What they are to you: the anchor (正官)
7.text:
Since they arrived, you pay bills on time. You own a proper duvet. You are, somehow, an adult.

Yeon: {them} is your Anchor in saju's ten roles. Their element shapes yours. They bring structure and doing it properly.

Bom: You feel safer with them. Taken seriously.

Yeon: Sometimes also slightly supervised.

Bom: Say when the rope's too tight. Good anchors give some slack when asked.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Grown-up is good. Supervised is not. Say which one it feels like.

8.heading: What they are to you: the mystic (偏印)
8.text:
You've had a three-hour conversation about whether fish get bored. They didn't think it was a weird question. That's when you knew.

Bom: {them} is your Mystic in saju's ten roles. Their element feeds yours, in unusual ways. They see your strange parts and like them.

Yeon: Two people in a private world. Lovely. Also, when did you last leave the flat together?

Bom: Plan shared things, not only shared silences. A trip. A party. A project.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: They love the weird bits of you. Take those bits outside sometimes.

9.heading: What they are to you: the safe place (正印)
9.text:
You walk in, drop your bag, and your shoulders come down two inches. That's them. That's what they do to you.

Bom: {them} is your Nurturer in saju's ten roles. Their element feeds yours. Being with them feels like coming home.

Yeon: The risk is moving in emotionally and never going out again.

Bom: Let their care be a base, not a bubble. And look after them back, on purpose.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Home base, not a hiding place.

combo.heading: Your two types: a natural pull (天干合)
combo.text:
Your two types form one of saju's five "heavenly combinations": pairs that naturally bind. You probably felt it early. The "oh, it's you" feeling.

Yeon: A pull is not a free pass. You still have to do the dishes.

Bom: It does make coming back together easier after a fight. So get very good at the coming back part.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: The pull is real. Make repairing fast your house rule.

same_stem.heading: Your two types: exactly the same
same_stem.text:
You're the same type. Same instincts, same reactions, same face when the waiter brings the wrong dish.

Yeon: When one of you is low, you both sink. Two people on the same sofa, staring at the same wall.

Bom: Agree on a rescue ritual for low days. A walk, a favourite meal, a film. Whoever's less sunk drives.

Yeon: And find your differences on purpose. That's where the growing happens.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Same type. When one sinks, the other throws the rope.

same_element.heading: Your two types: same element, different volume
same_element.text:
You share an element, but one of you plays it loud and one plays it soft. Same core, different speakers.

Bom: The louder one usually leads in public. The softer one leads at home.

Yeon: Stop trying to convert each other. Nobody's switching volume after twenty-five years of practice.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Same heart, different volume. Both are right.

generating.heading: Your two types: one feeds the other
generating.text:
In saju's cycle, one of your elements feeds the other. One gives, one grows. It feels nourishing.

Yeon: Quick test: who planned the last three dates? That's the feeder.

Bom: Swap now and then on purpose. The giver needs receiving, and the receiver grows by giving.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Feeder and fed. Swap roles before someone runs dry.

controlling.heading: Your two types: you keep each other in check
controlling.text:
In saju's cycle, one of your elements checks the other. You spot each other's flaws instantly. You also push each other to grow.

Yeon: It's friction. Useful friction. Like sandpaper with a crush.

Bom: It works best with clear roles. Who decides what. Drawn in advance, with a sense of humour.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You sharpen each other. Keep it kind and keep it funny.

clash.heading: Your two types: head-on
clash.text:
Your two types face each other directly. Saju calls it a clash. You'd call it "we're never bored".

Yeon: Debates over dinner. Fireworks over parking. Somehow still holding hands after.

Bom: Point it outward. Push each other's ambitions. Take on a hard thing together.

Yeon: And set ground rules for arguments. No fighting dirty. No dragging up 2019.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Clash couples last when nobody fights dirty.

peer.heading: Your elements in a fight: two equals
peer.text:
You and {them} share an element. So your fights are two people who think they're right, in the exact same way.

Yeon: Standoff. Arms crossed. Nobody blinks. The cat leaves the room.

Bom: Let one person win the small ones, on purpose. Take turns.

Yeon: And when it starts, say "here we go, round forty-two". Laughing mid-fight breaks the spell faster than logic.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Same weight class. Take turns losing the small rounds.

output.heading: Your elements in a fight: the lecture
output.text:
Your element feeds {them_el}, theirs. So in a fight, you explain. Advise. Explain again with examples.

Yeon: They asked for a hug. You gave a TED talk.

Bom: Ask one question for every point you make. You'll find out what they're actually upset about.

Yeon: Spot your script in minute one, not minute twenty. "Oh no, I'm doing the lecture." Say it. They'll laugh.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Fewer slides, more questions.

wealth.heading: Your elements in a fight: the fixer
wealth.text:
Your element manages {them_el}, theirs. So in a fight, you go straight to fixing. You've solved it. You've assigned tasks.

Bom: They don't feel helped. They feel managed.

Yeon: Nobody wants a project plan when they're crying.

Bom: Ask "what do you need right now?" before you offer any solution. Then actually do that one.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Ask what they need before you fix anything.

power.heading: Your elements in a fight: feeling overruled
power.text:
{them_el}, their element, presses on yours. So in a fight you can feel pushed, judged, outvoted. Then you either swing hard or go silent.

Bom: Say "I feel pushed" early. It's information, not weakness.

Yeon: It also tends to change their tone in about four seconds. Very efficient sentence.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: "I feel pushed." Three words. Instant volume control.

resource.heading: Your elements in a fight: the comforter
resource.text:
{them_el}, their element, feeds yours. So even when they're the one who's upset, they somehow end up comforting you.

Yeon: They came to complain and left holding your hand and saying "it's okay". How.

Bom: Notice it. Make room for their hurt first, before yours.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: They comfort you mid-fight. Ask about their hurt before yours.

rat.heading: How you live at home: the Rat (子)
rat.text:
Your home life runs on inside jokes, 1am talks and a version of you nobody outside ever sees.

Bom: In saju this is your "spouse palace", the day branch: the Rat, midnight Water, a branch tied to charm.

Yeon: Privacy matters to you. A lot. A partner who reads your phone over your shoulder will not last the weekend.

Bom: You need someone who doesn't take your guarded moments personally. Your side of home, done. Below is how theirs meets it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Inside jokes and late-night privacy. That's your home.

ox.heading: How you live at home: the Ox (丑)
ox.text:
You want a home that's solid, a routine that holds, and a partner who's in it for the long haul.

Bom: Your spouse palace in saju is the Ox: cold Earth that stores Metal. Steady, devoted.

Yeon: Also immovable on how the dishwasher gets loaded. There is a right way. It is your way.

Bom: Pick your battles at home. That's your half. Theirs is coming up below.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Devoted. Also stubborn about the cutlery basket.

tiger.heading: How you live at home: the Tiger (寅)
tiger.text:
A home that feels like a cage makes you pace. You need doors that open, and a partner who'll grab their coat when you say "let's go".

Bom: Your spouse palace in saju is the Tiger: early spring Wood. Independent, adventurous.

Yeon: Commitment, yes. Curfew, absolutely not.

Bom: Freedom inside the commitment. That's your side. Here's how theirs fits in.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Freedom inside the commitment. Not instead of it.

rabbit.heading: How you live at home: the Rabbit (卯)
rabbit.text:
You want home to be gentle. Soft light, soft words, nobody slamming cupboards.

Bom: Your spouse palace in saju is the Rabbit: spring Wood, one of the charm branches. Tender, a bit romantic.

Yeon: A shouty argument in the kitchen will stay in your body for days. You'll still flinch at that cupboard.

Bom: You need a partner who's kind at home, not only in public. Your half, done. Their half is below.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Slam a cupboard near you and you'll remember it for a week.

dragon.heading: How you live at home: the Dragon (辰)
dragon.text:
You've planned the dream house. And the next one. And the one by the sea for when you're seventy.

Bom: Your spouse palace in saju is the Dragon: damp Earth that stores Water. A big inner life, big hopes for the two of you.

Yeon: You need a partner who takes the dreams seriously and doesn't flinch at a little intensity at breakfast.

Bom: That's your side of home. Here's how theirs meets it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Big dreams for two. Say them out loud at home.

snake.heading: How you live at home: the Snake (巳)
snake.text:
It took you ages to let them see your messy drawer. Now they know where everything is, including the secrets.

Bom: Your spouse palace in saju is the Snake: early summer Fire. Deep, loyal, private.

Yeon: Slow to open. Then fully open. Break your trust at home once and the door doesn't swing back easily.

Bom: Trust is everything for you here. That's your side. Their side is below.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Slow to open, then all in. Don't waste the key.

horse.heading: How you live at home: the Horse (午)
horse.text:
Music on. Friends over. A home that feels lived in, not tiptoed around.

Bom: Your spouse palace in saju is the Horse: midsummer Fire, a charm branch. Passionate, free.

Yeon: Try to tie you down and you'll be "just popping out" for the rest of the year.

Bom: A warm, lively home with an open door. That's yours. Theirs is below.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: A warm, loud home with the door open. That's you.

goat.heading: How you live at home: the Goat (未)
goat.text:
Fairy lights. A blanket on every chair. A half-finished craft project you'll definitely finish.

Bom: Your spouse palace in saju is the Goat: warm late-summer Earth. Gentle and creative.

Yeon: You need a partner who's kind and patient. And who doesn't call the craft project "clutter".

Bom: Cosy, artistic, slow. That's your half of home. Here's theirs.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Cosy, creative, patient. Hands off the craft corner.

monkey.heading: How you live at home: the Monkey (申)
monkey.text:
You need a home with banter in it. Bad puns. Debates about nothing. A partner who laughs at the joke and then makes a better one.

Bom: Your spouse palace in saju is the Monkey: early autumn Metal. Playful, sharp.

Yeon: Bore you at home and you'll start rearranging the furniture for fun. Or your life.

Bom: Keep each other laughing. That's your side. Their side is below.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Keep each other laughing. That's the whole maintenance plan.

rooster.heading: How you live at home: the Rooster (酉)
rooster.text:
You notice when a frame is crooked. You notice when the towels don't match. You notice.

Bom: Your spouse palace in saju is the Rooster: autumn Metal, one of the charm branches. Refined, orderly.

Yeon: You need a partner who appreciates the details. Or at least pretends very convincingly.

Bom: A beautiful, tidy home. That's your half. Here's how theirs fits.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Crooked frame? You saw it. You fixed it. Nobody noticed.

dog.heading: How you live at home: the Dog (戌)
dog.text:
You'd check the locks twice for them. You'd walk them to the car in the rain. You'd do it every time.

Bom: Your spouse palace in saju is the Dog: dry autumn Earth that keeps Fire. Loyal, protective.

Yeon: And you need that loyalty back. Not 80 percent. Full.

Bom: Devotion given and needed. That's your side of home. Theirs is below.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You'd guard their door forever. Make sure they'd guard yours.

pig.heading: How you live at home: the Pig (亥)
pig.text:
Full fridge. Big portions. A sofa that swallows guests whole.

Bom: Your spouse palace in saju is the Pig: early winter Water. Generous, easygoing, comfortable.

Yeon: You need a partner who enjoys simple pleasures with you. Not someone who's always "just checking emails".

Bom: An abundant, relaxed home. That's your half. Their half is below.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Snacks, blankets, no emails. Your ideal evening, honestly.

same.heading: Your two home styles: identical
same.text:
Your day branches are the same, so you want home the same way. Same bedtime, same snacks, same idea of a perfect Sunday.

Yeon: Very easy to live together. Very easy to fall into the same rut for four years.

Bom: Shake up a routine together now and then. Mornings and weekends decide how happy a couple feels more than any grand gesture.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Same home style. Easy. Shake it up once a season.

clash.heading: Your two home styles: opposite
clash.text:
Your day branches clash. Opposite animals. One of you is a 6am person, the other thinks 6am is a myth.

Bom: Saju reads it as friction in daily life. Different rhythms, different ideas of home.

Yeon: Not a dealbreaker. Homework.

Bom: Agree the household basics out loud. And give each other space when the rhythms collide. The small daily stuff matters more than the big romance.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Opposite rhythms. Agree the basics out loud.

harmony.heading: Your two home styles: a natural fit (六合)
harmony.text:
Your day branches are a "six-harmony" pair: two animals that naturally combine. Living together just clicks.

Bom: Your habits fit. Their mess goes where your tidy doesn't.

Yeon: Don't get smug. Ease is a gift, not a guarantee. Look after it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Daily life fits. Treasure it, don't coast on it.

trio.heading: Your two home styles: same team (三合)
trio.text:
Your day branches belong to the same "three-harmony" group: animals that share an element.

Bom: At home, you pull in the same direction. You back each other's goals.

Yeon: Translation: when one of you says "let's do it", the other is already getting the drill out.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Same team at home. Rare. Use it.

neutral.heading: Your two home styles: a blank page
neutral.text:
Your day branches are neutral. No pull, no clash.

Bom: Home will feel like whatever you build. Nothing in the chart builds it for you.

Yeon: So build it on purpose. Rituals don't appear because you both wished for one.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Blank page at home. Write your own rituals.

strong_strong.heading: You two, side by side: both built strong
strong_strong.text:
Two strong charts. Two people who both think their way is obviously the way.

Yeon: Aligned, you're a power couple. Not aligned, you're two people silently reorganising the same cupboard in opposite directions.

Bom: Split the territory. Who leads on money, who leads on holidays, who leads on the flat. Then stick to it.

Bom: Next chapter: how you grow together. Including the bit where one of you has to go second.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Two captains. Divide the ship before it sinks.

strong_weak.heading: You two, side by side: you lead, they adapt
strong_weak.text:
Your chart is the strong one, theirs is the soft one. You naturally lead. They naturally make room.

Bom: That can feel easy and harmonious.

Yeon: Or you steamroll them and they let you, and you both call it "we just agree on everything".

Bom: Ask their opinion first on anything that affects you both. First, not after you've decided.

Yeon: Next: how you grow together. Hint, it involves you sitting in the passenger seat.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Ask what they think before you decide. Not after.

weak_strong.heading: You two, side by side: they lead, you adapt
weak_strong.text:
Their chart is the strong one, yours is the soft one. They lead. You adapt.

Yeon: It feels safe. Then one day you realise every film for two years was their pick.

Bom: Keep saying what you'd like, even the small stuff. Especially the small stuff.

Bom: Next chapter: growing together, and the part of it that's yours to start.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Pick the film. Every so often. Out loud.

weak_weak.heading: You two, side by side: both built soft
weak_weak.text:
Two soft charts. You're both kind, considerate, and very, very slow at deciding where to eat.

Yeon: "I don't mind, you pick." "No, you pick." Forty minutes. Both starving.

Bom: Take turns being the decider. Mondays you, Thursdays them. Home stays gentle and dinner actually happens.

Yeon: Next: how you two grow together. Someone has to go first. Spoiler, both of you.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Take turns deciding dinner. Kindness, but faster.

yang.heading: Your starting style: you go first
yang.text:
Your type is yang, the outward half. You suggest the plan, raise the issue, move things along.

Yeon: You're the "so, are we doing this or not" person.

Bom: Leave gaps for them to go first. Then wait. Longer than feels natural.

Bom: Last chapter next. The long run: what lasts, and what you two need to protect.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You start things. Leave room for them to start some.

yin.heading: Your starting style: you go deeper
yin.text:
Your type is yin, the inward half. You reflect, adjust, understand. You rarely kick things off.

Yeon: You've had the perfect idea for a trip for two years. They still don't know about it.

Bom: Start something yourself. Small is fine.

Yeon: And now the last chapter. The long run. Where this is all heading, if you both keep showing up.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You deepen things. Start one too. Small counts.

wood.heading: What they bring into your life: growth
wood.text:
Their element is Wood. With them, life keeps moving forward. Plans, goals, a "where do you see us in five years" over brunch.

Yeon: On tired days that feels like pressure. On good days it feels like someone believes in you.

Bom: Tell them which goals are real and which ones are happy daydreams.

Bom: Next chapter: what you're carrying. Too much of one thing, none of another, and why they've noticed before you did.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: They believe in where you're going. Tell them where that is.

fire.heading: What they bring into your life: warmth
fire.text:
Their element is Fire. With them, you get celebrated. Birthdays matter. Wins get toasted. Friends get invited over.

Yeon: They also notice the exact second your warmth drops. Like a smoke alarm, but for affection.

Bom: Laugh at their jokes. Say thank you where people can hear.

Yeon: Coming up: what you bring to this. Some of it is lovely. One part of it, they're quietly tired of.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: They celebrate you loudly. Clap back.

earth.heading: What they bring into your life: solid ground
earth.text:
Their element is Earth. With them, there's always milk in the fridge and someone calm when the boiler breaks.

Bom: They remember your mum's birthday. They remember your dentist.

Yeon: And they never ask for credit, and quietly wish for it every day.

Bom: Next: what you're carrying, too much and too little. It's the reason they feel so steadying to you.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Say thank you for the milk. It's never just milk.

metal.heading: What they bring into your life: clarity
metal.text:
Their element is Metal. With them, you always know where you stand. On the haircut, the job offer and the friend who's using you.

Yeon: Truth with no wrapping paper. Free of charge. Whether you asked or not.

Bom: That honesty is protection. You can still ask for a softer delivery on rough days.

Yeon: Next chapter: what you're overloaded with and what you're missing. They've probably told you already. Bluntly.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: They tell you the truth because they're on your side. Mostly.

water.heading: What they bring into your life: depth
water.text:
Their element is Water. With them, conversations go somewhere. You've seen your own life from angles you didn't know existed.

Yeon: They also vanish mid-sentence into their own head and come back twenty minutes later with "anyway".

Bom: Ask where they went. They love being asked. It's where the best talks start.

Bom: Next chapter: what you bring to the table, and the one thing your chart left off it.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Ask where their mind went. Best question you've got.

spring.heading: What you bring home: fresh starts
spring.text:
You were born in spring, so you rearrange the furniture when you're restless. New plants. A sudden plan to paint the bedroom green.

Yeon: Home life stands still for two months and you start looking at flats online.

Bom: Agree on a small yearly refresh. You don't need a new address to feel new.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: A yearly refresh, not a new postcode.

summer.heading: What you bring home: a party
summer.text:
You were born in summer, so your ideal home has friends in it. Music on. Doors open. Someone always staying for one more drink.

Bom: A quieter partner may need some nights that are just the two of you.

Yeon: Party house four nights. Sacred nights in, three. Negotiate from there.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Party house, plus a few sacred nights in.

autumn.heading: What you bring home: order
autumn.text:
You were born in autumn, so things have places and the year has rituals. Big seasonal dinners. A proper clear-out.

Yeon: A messy partner is your personal test from the heavens.

Bom: Pick two zones that stay tidy. Let the rest go. Peace in exchange for one drawer of chaos.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Two tidy zones. Chaos allowed elsewhere. Peace treaty.

winter.heading: What you bring home: a den
winter.text:
You were born in winter, so home is your den. Warm, quiet, safe from everyone. It's where you refill.

Bom: A social partner might fill it with people.

Yeon: Agree on how often guests come, so your den stays yours too. Otherwise you'll start hiding in the bathroom at your own dinner party.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: The den is your charger. Guard the plug.

earth.heading: What you bring home: steadiness
earth.text:
You were born in the in-between weeks, so you're the steady one at home through every change. Moves, new jobs, renovations, a puppy.

Yeon: You hold it together so well that nobody else learned how.

Bom: Let them lead the next big change. You don't always have to carry the boxes.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Steady in every move. Let them carry some boxes.

peer.heading: What you bring to the two of you: your own self
peer.text:
Your chart's loudest element is your own. So you stay you inside the relationship, and you expect them to stay them.

Bom: That keeps you from melting into one blurry couple person. Healthy.

Yeon: It can also read as "doesn't need me". Offer closeness as easily as you take space.

Yeon: Now the fun part. How you two fight. I've been waiting for this one.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You stay yourself. Let them see that includes wanting them.

output.heading: What you bring to the two of you: sparkle
output.text:
Your chart's loudest element is expression. You bring affection, jokes, the little gestures. You make love visible.

Yeon: Mostly on birthdays, though. Weekdays get the budget version.

Bom: Spend some sparkle on a random Wednesday. It lands twice as hard.

Bom: Next: how you fight, and the move you pull every time that you think nobody's clocked.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Birthday-level effort on a Wednesday. Try it once.

wealth.heading: What you bring to the two of you: a life that works
wealth.text:
Your chart's loudest element is the practical one. Bills paid, plans happening, problems solved before breakfast.

Bom: They can rely on you completely.

Yeon: They'd also like one afternoon where nothing gets achieved. Not one thing.

Yeon: Coming up: how you two fight. Practical people fight about lists. Yours is very specific.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Schedule time with no purpose. Yes, schedule it.

power.heading: What you bring to the two of you: commitment
power.text:
Your chart's loudest element is duty. Promises kept, showing up, integrity. They never wonder if you'll come.

Yeon: Reliable. Respectable. A little bit like a very good bank.

Bom: Show them your silly side too. Reliability is even more lovable with a sense of humour.

Bom: Next chapter: how you fight. Spoiler, the reliable one is not always the reasonable one.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You always show up. Show up goofy sometimes.

resource.heading: What you bring to the two of you: understanding
resource.text:
Your chart's loudest element is understanding. Patience, insight, a calm voice when they're spiralling.

Bom: You read their inner world beautifully.

Yeon: Yours, though, is a locked diary. They've never seen page one.

Bom: Let them understand you back. Then turn the page, because next is how you two fight.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You understand them so well. Give them the chance to return it.

output.heading: What to steal from them: their words
output.text:
Your chart runs low on expression. So steal their way of saying what they feel.

Bom: Copy one habit. A nightly "best part of today". A text when they miss you. A compliment said out loud.

Yeon: Plagiarism, but romantic. Totally allowed.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Borrow their words. Say one feeling a day.

wealth.heading: What to steal from them: their drive
wealth.text:
Your chart is short on the "make it happen" element. So borrow their drive.

Yeon: Let them drag you into plans. Then shock everyone and lead one shared project a year yourself.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Borrow their drive. Then run one project yourself.

power.heading: What to steal from them: their routines
power.text:
Your chart is short on the structure element. So borrow their reliability habits. Calendars. Routines. Small promises kept.

Bom: It makes the relationship feel safe, for both of you.

Yeon: Yes, even the shared calendar. Especially the shared calendar.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Steal their calendar habit. Small promises feel like safety.

resource.heading: What to steal from them: their rest
resource.text:
Your chart is short on the support element. So borrow their talent for resting and being looked after.

Yeon: They can lie on a sofa for three hours guilt-free. Study them. It's a skill.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Steal their sofa skills. Slow mornings are a talent.

none.heading: What to steal from them: their certainty
none.text:
Your chart has every element in it, so you can fit almost anyone. What's worth borrowing is their certainty about what they want.

Bom: Let their clarity help you name your own preferences more often.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Borrow their certainty. Say what you want, first.

gap-wood.text:
You never ask for reassurance, so they assume you don't need it. You do. The sentence that lands deepest for you: "I've got this one. You can rest."

Yeon: Being told you're strong just adds weight. You've heard it your whole life.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Ask for relief by name. "Can you take this one?"

gap-wood.heading: The sentence you need to hear

eul-wood.text:
You adjust to everyone, so the sentence that melts you is: "What do YOU want?" Asked like they actually want the answer.

Yeon: You'll say "I don't mind". They should ask again. You do mind.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: "What do you want?" Asked twice. That's your love language.

eul-wood.heading: The sentence you need to hear

byeong-fire.text:
You light up everyone, so the line you need is: "I see how much you give." Not thanks for the party. Recognition of the effort under it.

Yeon: You'll act like you don't need it. You'll replay it for a month.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You need to be noticed noticing. Ask for that.

byeong-fire.heading: The sentence you need to hear

jeong-fire.text:
You give quiet, close attention, so you need it back in the same size: "I remembered." The small detail. The thing you mentioned once in March.

Yeon: A grand gesture won't move you half as much as them knowing your order.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Small remembered things are your proof of love.

jeong-fire.heading: The sentence you need to hear

mu-earth.text:
You hold everything up, so the sentence you need is: "You don't have to hold it all." Said while they actually take something off your plate.

Yeon: Words without the plate thing don't count. You'll notice.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Mountains need a day off too. Ask for one.

mu-earth.heading: The sentence you need to hear

gi-earth.text:
You look after everyone, so what you need is to be looked after back. "Sit. I'll do it." Tea you didn't make. A plan you didn't organise.

Yeon: You'll try to help them help you. Don't. Sit.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Sit down. Let the tea be made for you. Once.

gi-earth.heading: The sentence you need to hear

gyeong-metal.text:
You protect everyone, so the line that gets you is: "I'm on your side." Out loud, especially when you were the one being difficult.

Yeon: You'll pretend it doesn't affect you. Your shoulders will drop two inches.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Swords want loyalty, not compliments. Ask for loyalty.

gyeong-metal.heading: The sentence you need to hear

sin-metal.text:
You hold yourself to impossible standards, so you need: "You don't have to get it right with me." Permission to be messy and still adored.

Yeon: You'll argue with it. Let them say it anyway.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You're allowed to be unpolished with your person.

sin-metal.heading: The sentence you need to hear

im-water.text:
You need room, so the line you need is: "Go. I'll be here." Freedom that doesn't come with a guilt trip.

Yeon: Give you space without sulking, and you'll come back faster than anyone expects.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Hold an ocean loosely and it keeps coming back.

im-water.heading: The sentence you need to hear

gye-water.text:
You feel everything and say little, so what you need is: "Tell me. I won't rush you." Patience for the slow version of your feelings.

Yeon: Push you and you'll say "nothing". Wait, and you'll say everything.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Rain needs time to soak in. Ask for that time.

gye-water.heading: The sentence you need to hear

gap-wood.text:
You booked the table, checked the weather and know a backup bar in case the first is full.

Yeon: Romantic. Also a bit like a work trip.

Bom: Your best dates are the ones where you hand over control. A surprise picnic you didn't plan. "Just get in the car."

Yeon: And as a couple, you bond side by side. A hike with a summit. A flat-pack shelf with too many screws. Always have one shared project going.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Hand over one evening. Let them steer the pine.

gap-wood.heading: Date night, Pine edition: you planned it

eul-wood.text:
You noticed the lighting, the music, and that their chair wobbles. Before you'd sat down.

Bom: You make ordinary places feel special. A flower market, a tiny café, a walk with no destination.

Yeon: And you'll remember what they ordered for the next ten years.

Bom: You grow through little rituals more than big events. The same Sunday bakery. The song you always play in the car.

Yeon: If they're a grand-gesture person, deal: they plan the big trip, you bring the small rituals that make it yours.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Same bakery every Sunday. Love climbs by repetition.

eul-wood.heading: Date night, Flower edition: small and pretty

byeong-fire.text:
You befriended the waiter, invented a game about the other diners and suggested a second venue before dessert.

Yeon: They're never bored. They are sometimes exhausted.

Bom: Build in one quiet stretch. The walk home. A bench. Ten minutes with no plan, so they can catch up and talk.

Yeon: You're also natural hosts. Dinners, birthdays, a full house. Agree on a ratio with a quieter partner. Two social weekends, one at home.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Build a quiet bit into every date. Ten minutes, no plan.

byeong-fire.heading: Date night, Sun edition: you're the show

jeong-fire.text:
Corner table. Low light. A conversation that goes somewhere real. Loud clubs are not dates to you. They're events.

Bom: You're happiest when the evening turns into a memory. The night you talked until the café closed.

Yeon: You need regular one-on-one time that isn't about logistics. Phones in a drawer. Actual questions.

Bom: "What's been on your mind?" is a whole date for you. If they're more of an action person, take turns: their night out, your night in.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Phones in a drawer, one real question. That's the date.

jeong-fire.heading: Date night, Candle edition: one table, one real talk

mu-earth.text:
You drove, you paid attention, and you ordered the dish they liked last time without asking.

Bom: Your ideal date is unhurried. Long dinner, slow walk, nowhere to be.

Yeon: Three venues in one evening and you're quietly dying. You'll go anyway, to be nice.

Bom: Your love letter is security. But they might need surprises too.

Yeon: Schedule spontaneity if you have to. One unplanned day a month where you say yes to everything. Mountains can host a festival. They just like a date in the diary.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: One unplanned day a month. Put it in the diary. Ironically.

mu-earth.heading: Date night, Mountain edition: slow and unhurried

gi-earth.text:
You checked they were warm enough, shared your chips and asked about their mum's knee.

Bom: Your ideal date involves food made with love. Cooking together. A market. A homemade picnic.

Yeon: Fancy restaurants are fine. A meal you both burnt slightly together is better.

Bom: You build home fast. Shared shelf, favourite mug, weekly dinner, all within months.

Yeon: Leave the house sometimes. A weekend away. A gig. An evening where nobody needs feeding.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Leave the house. Nobody needs feeding tonight.

gi-earth.heading: Date night, Garden edition: food made with love

gyeong-metal.text:
You picked the place, made the call, and handled it when they lost the booking. Smoothly.

Bom: They feel so safe with you.

Yeon: Your ideal date has a bit of challenge in it. Climbing. An escape room. A board game you fully intend to win.

Bom: You love by fixing and improving. The bike, the bills, standing up for them at a family dinner.

Yeon: Improvement can sound like criticism. Ask first: "Want my two cents, or just my company?" Saves a lot of unnecessary cuts.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: "Two cents or just company?" Ask before improving anything.

gyeong-metal.heading: Date night, Sword edition: a challenge to win

sin-metal.text:
You chose the restaurant, the outfit and the playlist for the drive. It was, objectively, perfect.

Bom: Your taste is a gift. They feel lucky to be shown your world.

Yeon: If they shrug at the effort, though? Very cool evening. Frosty dessert.

Bom: Tell them it matters to you. And sometimes, let a date be ugly. Rain, takeaway, a terrible film.

Yeon: Laughing through a ruined plan together is one of the best bonds a jewel can get.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Let one date go wrong. Laugh through it. That's the polish.

sin-metal.heading: Date night, Jewel edition: curated

im-water.text:
A neighbourhood you've never been to. A dish neither of you can pronounce. A train to a random town.

Yeon: Routine dates feel like a puddle to you.

Bom: Your ideal date ends with a conversation that's still going at 1am.

Yeon: A homebody partner can feel left on the platform. Bring them at their pace.

Bom: And stay in sometimes with a curious mind. A new recipe, a documentary, a question you've never asked. A night in can be an adventure too.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Unknown streets, unpronounceable food, talk past midnight.

im-water.heading: Date night, Ocean edition: somewhere new

gye-water.text:
You clocked their mood before they mentioned it, swapped to a quieter café and ordered extra dessert. No discussion.

Bom: Your ideal date is cosy with a bit of magic. A film in the rain. A late-night snack run. A secret spot only you know.

Yeon: You two build private worlds. Nicknames, inside jokes, a show nobody else watches.

Bom: Precious. Make sure the big talks happen too. Plans, money, the future.

Yeon: They feel heavy. Having them early keeps the cosy world safe from surprises.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Inside jokes are sacred. Big talks too. Do both.

gye-water.heading: Date night, Rain edition: cosy with a bit of magic

strong.heading: How you say sorry
strong.text:
Your apology comes with a plan attached. "You're right, I was wrong, here's what I'll change." Solid. And it can still miss.

Bom: They need the feeling before the fix. Proof you felt it, not just solved it.

Yeon: Slow down by one sentence. "You were waiting and felt like you didn't matter." Then shut up for a second.

Bom: Let them correct you. The fix lands softer once they feel understood.

Yeon: And no relitigating ten minutes later. Let the sorry stand for one whole evening.

Bom: Next chapter, we read your own story back to you. How long, what you fight about. It explains a lot of what you just read.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Feeling first, fix second. One sentence about how it was for them.

weak.heading: How you say sorry
weak.text:
You've apologised for things that weren't your fault. You've apologised for apologising.

Yeon: "Sorry" as a fire extinguisher. Anything to make the bad feeling stop.

Bom: Over-sorrying means they stop hearing it, and the real issue never gets a turn.

Yeon: Two-part rule. Sorry only for what you did. Then your need: "I'm sorry I snapped. I was hurt you cancelled again."

Bom: And when they apologise, take it. Don't say "it's nothing". If it hurt, it wasn't nothing.

Yeon: Next page: your story, read back to you. You told us more than you think.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Own your part. Name your need. Both halves count.

wood.heading: A home ritual that steadies you: growing something
wood.text:
Your chart steadies with Wood, the growing element. So your best ritual is growing something together. A plant you both keep alive. A walk in the same park every week, watching it change.

Bom: Once a season, grab a notebook and write three things to try as a couple. Cross them off slowly.

Yeon: The list isn't the point. Feeling like you're both still going somewhere is.

Bom: Next chapter is the one Yeon's been dying to write: your blind spot in love.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Once a season: one notebook, three new things to try.

fire.heading: A home ritual that steadies you: warmth
fire.text:
