Your chart steadies with Fire, the warm element. So your best ritual is warmth. A candle at dinner. Music while you cook. Friends over once a month, even if the flat is a mess.

Bom: Celebrate small wins out loud. A finished project. The first coffee on the balcony after winter.

Yeon: Couples who celebrate small things argue less about big ones. There's warmth in the bank.

Yeon: Next: your blind spot. I have notes. Many notes.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Celebrate the small wins. Warmth in the bank.

earth.heading: A home ritual that steadies you: routine
earth.text:
Your chart steadies with Earth, the grounding element. So your best ritual is routine. Same Saturday breakfast. A shared food shop. A Sunday evening reset where you tidy for twenty minutes and plan the week.

Yeon: Sounds unromantic. Isn't. Predictable time together is what love grows in.

Bom: Guard it even in busy weeks. Your chart relaxes when the ground is steady.

Bom: Next chapter: your blind spot in love. Yeon wrote this one. Be brave.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Sunday reset: twenty minutes tidying, ten minutes planning.

metal.heading: A home ritual that steadies you: clearing
metal.text:
Your chart steadies with Metal, the clarifying element. So your best ritual is clearing. Once a month, fifteen minutes: one thing that's working, one thing to change. Kind, short, then dessert.

Yeon: Clear one shelf or one obligation together too. A tidy drawer and a clear conversation do the same job for you.

Bom: They cut the noise. Then you can hear each other.

Yeon: Coming up: your blind spot. Bring a cushion to hold.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Monthly: one thing working, one thing to change. Then dessert.

water.heading: A home ritual that steadies you: slowing down
water.text:
Your chart steadies with Water, the reflective element. So your best ritual is slow talk. A late tea. A walk by the river about anything except logistics.

Bom: And protect one fully lazy morning a week. No plans, no chores, just drifting together.

Yeon: It looks like doing nothing. For your chart, it's how the well refills.

Bom: Next: your blind spot in love. It's softer than you'd expect. Mostly.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: One lazy morning a week, together. That's the refill.

peer.heading: One Sunday with the two of you
peer.text:
You share an element, so your Sundays run on the same clock. Long breakfast, or early run. Nobody negotiates.

Yeon: Lovely. Also the same café, the same show and the same walk since forever.

Bom: Once a month, one of you picks something the other would never choose. Small surprise, new thing to talk about over Monday dinner.

Bom: That's us. Read this together tonight and fight about who's more like their chapter. We'll be here.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Same clock, same café. Once a month, pick something weird.

output.heading: One Sunday with the two of you
output.text:
Your element feeds theirs, so on Sundays you make it nice. The plan, the brunch, the playlist. They bloom.

Yeon: And you end the weekend knackered while they end it refreshed. Hmm.

Bom: Swap every other Sunday. Let them pick, even if it's a strange museum and cold noodles.

Yeon: Being on the receiving end shows you how they love. That's the last lesson. Go and let them plan something.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Every other Sunday, they plan. Cold noodles included.

wealth.heading: One Sunday with the two of you
wealth.text:
Your element shapes theirs, so on Sundays you steer. When to leave, which errands, which friends.

Bom: They often like being steered. The day runs beautifully.

Yeon: Make sure it's their day too. Ask first thing: "What would make today good for you?" Then build around it.

Bom: That question is our goodbye present. Ask it this Sunday and see what you learn.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Ask what a good day looks like for them. Build from there.

power.heading: One Sunday with the two of you
power.text:
Their element shapes yours, so on Sundays they set the pace and you go along. Some weeks that's exactly what you want.

Yeon: Other weeks you realise you haven't done one single thing you picked since August.

Bom: Claim a slot. Two hours that are yours, said out loud, in advance. They'll respect a clear ask far more than a quiet sulk.

Yeon: Final note from us: tell them what you want. They're probably relieved to finally know.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Two hours that are yours, booked out loud. Not a sulk.

resource.heading: One Sunday with the two of you
resource.text:
Their element feeds yours, so a Sunday with them means being looked after. Breakfast made. Plan sorted. Sofa already warm.

Bom: Enjoy it. Then give back in your own currency. Fix the thing they mentioned. Plan next weekend. Take them somewhere they've wanted to go.

Yeon: Say thank you with actions, not just "aw, thanks babe".

Bom: That's the whole reading. Now go and be lovely to each other. Out loud.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: They spoil you. Thank them with something you do, not something you say.

new.speaker: bom
new.text: Under a year. Still in the part where you learn how they take their coffee and what their silence means.

settled.speaker: yeon
settled.text: One to three years. The honeymoon left, the real people moved in. This is where it gets interesting.

long.speaker: bom
long.text: Three-plus years. You can read their mood from the sound of the keys in the door.

committed.speaker: yeon
committed.text: Engaged or married. So you've signed up for the long version. Let's make sure you both read the manual.

unsaid.speaker: bom
unsaid.text: You didn't say how long. Doesn't matter. Whether it's month two or year ten, the patterns are already there.

time.speaker: yeon
time.text: You fight about time and attention. Translation: one of you is saying "I miss you" in the angriest possible way.

logistics.speaker: yeon
logistics.text: Chores, plans, money stuff. Nobody's really fighting about the dishes. Nobody has ever really fought about the dishes.

feelings.speaker: bom
feelings.text: Feelings and communication. So you both care enough to argue about how you talk. That's actually a good sign.

people.speaker: yeon
people.text: Friends or family. Ah. The fight where you're both defending someone who isn't even in the room.

unsaid.speaker: bom
unsaid.text: You skipped what you fight about. Maybe you don't fight much. Or maybe it's the thing nobody says.

strength_titles.strong: Your blind spot: you push too hard
strength_titles.weak: Your blind spot: you give too much

gap-wood.how-you-love:
When you commit, you commit to the whole person and the whole future. You're the one with soup when they're sick and a plan when they're lost.

Yeon: And a slight attitude when they don't follow the plan.

Bom: You show love by building. Every fixed thing is an "I love you".

Yeon: Translate it once in a while. Some people need the words, not just the shelf.
gap-wood.how-you-fight:
You've opened a fight with "I just think it's fair to point out". Nobody has ever relaxed after that sentence.

Bom: You fight for what's fair. A broken promise, an uneven chore split, a careless comment.

Yeon: You don't scream. You explain. Calmly. Three times. Like a lawyer who's also disappointed in you.

Bom: The trouble is winning becomes the goal, and they end up feeling lectured instead of heard.

Yeon: Then you want closure in ten minutes. A handshake. An action plan. Minutes of the meeting.

Bom: Lead with "I'm sorry it got heated". Save the action plan for tomorrow morning. Same result, half the tension.

Yeon: Remember you're on the same side. The pine is against the wind, not the person standing under it.
gap-wood.growing-together:
You've mapped out the next decade for the two of you. Do they know they're in it?

Bom: You grow by building something together. A home, a project, traditions you invented on purpose.

Yeon: You need direction in love like you need it at work. Goals, revisited yearly. Like rings in a trunk.

Bom: You also grow when they trust you with something that matters to them. A big decision. A family mess.

Yeon: Just make sure it's not only you helping them. Let them drag you toward rest, play and things with no point at all.

Bom: A pine that only grows taller forgets to spread its branches.
gap-wood.long-term:
Picture you two at seventy. You're still arguing about the best route to the coast. You're still right.

Bom: Long term, you're a keeper. Loyal, consistent, willing to work through the hard years.

Yeon: The risk over decades is rigidity. How you did things at thirty becoming the only way at fifty.

Bom: They'll change, too. The person they are at forty might want different things from the one you met.

Yeon: Ask your first-date questions again, years later. Listen to the new answers like they're news. Because they are.

gap-wood.speaker: bom
gap-wood.text: The tall pine in love. Steady, protective, in it for decades.

gap-wood.speaker: yeon
gap-wood.text: Also has a five-year plan for the relationship. Did you show them the plan? Or just start building?

gap-wood.speaker: bom
gap-wood.text: You love by providing. Shelter, plans, a fixed tap. It's your whole heart, in practical form.

gap-wood.speaker: yeon
gap-wood.text: You've already planned their next five years. Have you asked what they wanted?

gap-wood.speaker: yeon
gap-wood.text: You don't raise your voice. You raise your points. Numbered.

gap-wood.speaker: yeon
gap-wood.text: There's a "correct" way to fold a fitted sheet. It's yours. Apparently.

spring.intro: Spring birthday. That's tree season, so you got a double shot of yourself: taller, louder, surer. In saju terms, Wood ran the month you were born in. In real life, you've never once waited to be picked.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Double Wood. So the stubbornness is seasonal AND personal. Great.

summer.intro: You're a tree born in the heat. All that growing goes straight into showing: big plans, big talk, big gestures. Summer burns through a pine fast, so you look unstoppable right up until you suddenly need three days in bed.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You give off so much light. Just save a little for yourself.

earth.intro: Born in the between-season weeks, when soil runs the show. For a tree, that means work: you're always building, fixing, providing. Very useful. Very tired. Somebody should ask what you want for once.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Rest is not a prize you win. It's allowed.

autumn.intro: Autumn is axe season, and you're the tree. Life started trimming you early: rules, pressure, people with opinions. It made you sharper and more disciplined than other pines. It also made you allergic to being told what to do.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Pruned young. Explains the posture. And the attitude.

winter.intro: A winter pine. The cold kept you quiet on the outside while the roots drank everything. You think longer than you let on, and when you finally move, it's because you already decided weeks ago.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You look calm. Underneath, you've been planning since November.

gap-wood.strong:
You've said "I'll just do it myself" in a tone. More than once. This week.

Yeon: Strong chart, Pine. Firm opinions, endless stamina, a roadmap for both of you nobody else has seen.

Bom: You're a steady, confident partner. People build on you.

Yeon: Blind spot: pushing. Deciding for two. Assuming your way of doing holidays is just "the normal way".

Bom: Make agreements together, out loud, and revisit them. Let them hold the pen sometimes.
gap-wood.weak:
You'd never admit you need reassurance. You'd also reread their last text four times to check it was warm enough.

Bom: Soft chart, Pine. You're tuned into them in ways they don't even notice.

Yeon: Blind spot: giving too much. Swallowing your preferences until resentment grows rings.

Bom: Ask for reassurance plainly. It's not needy. It's information they can actually use.

gap-wood.title: You love like a five-year plan. They'd like to see the plan.
gap-wood.text:
You're the one who books the holiday, remembers the insurance, and has a quiet opinion on where you'll both live in 2030.

Bom: You make them feel safe.

Yeon: You also make every decision before they've finished their sentence.
gap-wood.end: Bom: And how you love is only half of it. The other half is the thing you never ask for. Next page.

cliff.gap-wood: Yeon: Now, who you're actually with. Because they're not who you | think they are, and they've been dropping hints for a while.

gap-wood.speaker: yeon
gap-wood.text: Grow together means sometimes they lead. Yes, even with the map upside down.
